evidence.description: The shared singleton instance uses `MainActor.assumeIsolated` inside a `nonisolated(unsafe)` static property initializer, which can lead to runtime crashes if the isolation is not correctly assumed.

candidates.explanation: Using `MainActor.assumeIsolated` in a static initializer is risky. If the thread executing the initialization is not the main thread (which is common for static initializers), the app will crash. A safer approach would be to use a thread-safe initialization pattern or ensure the property is accessed only on the main actor.
candidates.title: Unsafe MainActor Assumption in Static Initializer

evidence.description: NotificationCenter observer uses a Task to call an async method on self, but the closure captures self weakly and then the Task captures the notification.
NotificationCenter observer for user profile updates uses a Task to call an async method on self.
NotificationCenter observer for seed progress updates uses a Task to call an async method on self.

candidates.explanation: While using `Task` inside a `NotificationCenter` observer is a common way to bridge to async code, these specific implementations do not provide any mechanism to cancel the tasks if the object is deallocated, potentially leading to execution of logic on a stale object or unnecessary work.
candidates.title: Unbounded Task Creation in Observers

evidence.description: The animateBalanceChange method uses nested DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter calls to manage animation state.

candidates.explanation: Using `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter` for managing state transitions and animations is an anti-pattern in modern Swift Concurrency. It creates 'callback hell' and makes the flow of state changes difficult to reason about. Since the class is already marked `@MainActor`, these should ideally be handled using `Task.sleep` or a more robust state machine.
candidates.title: Nested DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter for State Management

evidence.description: handleUserProfileUpdate is marked @MainActor but creates a new Task { @MainActor in } to update isLoggedIn.

candidates.explanation: The method `handleUserProfileUpdate` is already marked with `@MainActor`. Creating a new `Task { @MainActor in ... }` inside it is redundant and adds unnecessary overhead to the execution flow.
candidates.title: Redundant MainActor Task
